## Alternatives rejected

Filtering entries to `user`/`assistant` at render, as the issue text says, was dropped for the merged spec's FR-093, since Bowman already hides thinking entries. Importing HAL's frame types from `@re-cinq/hal-engine` would drag every provider SDK into the browser, so the types are copied and the recorder catches drift. Clearing the transcript on reconnect was simpler, but #14 requires it to stay on screen. Offering the access token as the subprotocol leaves it visible in the handshake until hal-engine#150 lands; the alternative, a short-lived ticket endpoint just for the socket, is more machinery than the PoC needs.

## Verification

Lint, typecheck, test and build pass at the root, with 100% coverage in both workspaces (44 api tests, 71 web tests). Breaking the r…

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `halSocket` takes a `WebSocketCtor` defaulting to `globalThis.WebSocket`, opens `new WebSocketCtor(url, [token])`, reconnects exactly once after a close with code 1006, and a second unclean close leaves the connection state `error` without opening a third socket
- [ ] A reconnect renders `Toast` with a Danish message stating the conversation was restarted, and the existing transcript stays on screen
- [ ] `apps/api/src/testing/recordWsFrames.ts` starts the engine on `provider: {type: 'mock'}`, sends `user_message` content `hej`, records every frame with `timestamp` normalized to `"<ts>"`, and writes `apps/web/src/chat/__fixtures__/hal-frames.json`
- [ ] The committed fixture is exactly nine frames in order: `connected`; user upsert at index 0; assistant upsert…

## Implements

- [**FR-214**: Lapsed with #181, which removed the frame recorder. While it existe…](https://github.com/re-cinq/otto/blob/46245fd4201a00105b31dee36bd17fa775cf9e64/specs/support-agent-chat/spec.md#L442)

## What to do

Work is confined to `re-cinq/Otto`, touching `044`'s files plus the two later tests that replay its fixture. Delete `apps/web/src/chat/__fixtures__/hal-frames.json` and `apps/api/src/testing/recordWsFrames.ts` along with the CI step that re-runs the recorder. Add `@re-cinq/hal-engine` to `apps/web/package.json` under `devDependencies` only - `044`'s total import ban is narrowed rather than lifted: since `066` made the provider peers optional and a `*.test.*` file ships in no bundle, test files may now import the package while the CI grep still fails on any value or type import in shipped code under `apps/web/src/`. The replay becomes the drift gate the deleted recorder used to be - a protocol change in a future engine release now fails the reducer tests in this repo's CI wit…

## Why

The `.catch` on the WebSocket upgrade chain answers any failure with `rejectSocket`, which writes an HTTP status line and destroys the stream - correct while the promise can only fail during authentication, but wrong for anything that fails after `wss.handleUpgrade` has already succeeded, since the same `.catch` also covers session creation, sending the `connected` frame, and a queued resume lookup. Measured directly on this repo's WebSocket library: a synchronous throw from a `connection` listener propagates into this `.catch`, which then writes an HTTP status line into a live WebSocket stream. The client sees `open`, the `connected` frame, then a frame-corruption error, then an unexplained close code `1006` - a protocol-corruption failure on a connection that had already succeede…

Link: https://github.com/re-cinq/Otto/commit/8834b9ba4d4a7d855e68265ccec0341c8aab2716

Replace the frame recorder and fixture with HAL Engine's recordedFrames

Otto's own recorder booted the api, sent "hej" and committed the frames
to a JSON fixture that tests loaded through an `as` cast, so the copied
wire types in protocol.ts were never checked against the engine and only
one scenario was ever replayed. HAL Engine 0.10.0 exports recordedFrames,
re-recorded by its own CI, so the replay test now assigns those frames to
the local union without a cast and covers a plain answer, thinking then a
tool, a suppressed round with an entry_skip, and a rate-limit error.

[2] "commit-8834b9ba4d4a7d855e68265ccec0341c8aab2716" section 2:
The recorder, its test, the fixture and the record-frames script are
gone. The disclosure test and the browser happy scenario derive their
expected strings from the replayed frames; the fixture server builds its
conversation_list row from the replayed turn, since the engine records no
list. The CI import ban now lets *.test.ts and *.test.tsx import the
engine and fails on a runtime dependency; @re-cinq/hal-engine is a web
devDependency only. The spec statements the fixture bound are marked
lapsed and the #181 statements cited. Gaps found on the way are #430.

Issue #181.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5.1 <noreply@anthropic.com>
